<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def clusters(f):
    g=f.ascii.split('\n')
    cs=[(r,c) for r in range(64) for c in range(64) if g[r][c]=='c']
    groups=[]
    for p in sorted(cs):
        for gr in groups:
            if abs(p[0]-gr[-1][0])<=3 and abs(p[1]-gr[-1][1])<=3: gr.append(p); break
        else: groups.append([p])
    out=[]
    for gr in groups:
        rr=[q[0] for q in gr]; cc=[q[1] for q in gr]
        out.append(((min(rr)+max(rr))//2,(min(cc)+max(cc))//2,len(gr)))
    return sorted(out)
for i,t in enumerate(transitions):
    b=clusters(t.before_frame); a=clusters(t.after_frame)
    if t.after_frame.level==t.before_frame.level and len(a)<len(b):
        gone=[x for x in b if x not in a]
        print(i,t.action,'L'+str(t.before_frame.level),'gone',gone)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
There are no transitions within the same level where the dot count decreased! In other words, in levels 1 and 2, dots were never "collected" during play. Then how did the level complete? The level must complete when all objects are placed in positions that cover all the dots — the game checks the final configuration, and the dots probably disappear upon level completion (the 10→8 at transition 101 was actually a level transition: the "before" of the level 2 frame had 10 gray clusters... no wait, before was level 2 with 10 clusters, after was level 3 with 8).
Hmm, wait, transition 101's before_frame.level: let me check. The before clusters were at (3,21),(9,27),(12,12),(36,27),(39,9),(42,24),(48,15),(48,33),(57,9),(60,27) — 10 clusters, some of size 6/8. That was the level 2 board (dots + probably plus endpoints). The after was the level 3 board with 8 dots.
So the level completes when... the last LEFT of level 2 (the plus coming to rest at (48,30)) triggered the level completion. At that point, were all the dots covered by the objects' final positions? Probably yes: the game evaluates the final placement — all dots lie on the outline of some object → level clear.
So the win condition: place all three objects so that every dot lies on the outline of some object, then... the level probably auto-completes when the last dot becomes covered (the moment the last object comes to rest). In level 2, the last move completed the cover → level clear.
Currently: the bar is at (6,24), covering (6,6),(6,45) — 2 out of 8 dots covered. The dots remain visible. Next, activate the X, move it to (24,42) to cover (15,51),(30,48),(33,33); then the diamond to (30,18) to cover (21,21),(27,9),(39,21) → all 8 covered → level 3 complete.
